The idea:

Yes. That's actually the cleanest architecture for your constraints. Your Windows PC doesn't need any Logitech software, scripts, drivers, or Store apps.

The Mac becomes the central controller:

                         ┌──────────────────────┐
                         │      LG 34U650A-B    │
                         └──────────▲───────────┘
                                    │
                              BetterDisplay
                                    │
                         ┌──────────┴───────────┐
                         │         Mac           │
                         │                       │
Windows ── curl ────────►│  Local HTTP server   │
                         │       :8080           │
                         │          │            │
                         │          ├─ LG → HDMI │
                         │          │             │
                         │          ├─ Logitech 1 │
                         │          │             │
                         │          └─ Logitech 1 │
                         └───────────────────────┘

And conversely, from the Mac you can call the same server:

curl http://localhost:8080/windows

or

curl http://localhost:8080/mac

Logitech Easy-Switch devices can only be switched from the machine they are currently connected to. This creates a key architectural constraint for the server design.

Several details still need clarification before building the server. The current input switching method via BetterDisplay CLI needs confirmation. The exact Easy-Switch channel mapping for Mac versus Windows must be known. The Logitech asymmetry constraint also needs clarification: whether switching to Windows requires Windows-side assistance or only Mac-side control.

The Mac server cannot control the Logitech device when Windows is the active host. Four possible solutions are being weighed: restricting server-side switching to display changes only, using a Logitech Flow receiver, accepting manual keyboard input, or having Windows run a small local helper.

The user explicitly wants Windows to send only curl requests to the Mac server. This means Windows cannot run any local helper scripts. The Mac server can handle BetterDisplay switching, but the Logitech Easy-Switch devices remain on Windows and cannot be controlled from the Mac. The only remaining question is whether the Logitech devices can be triggered through a different mechanism while Windows is the active host.

The Logitech ChangeHost command must be sent directly to the device while it is physically connected. This confirms that Windows must remain the active host to trigger the switch. The user's earlier statement that Windows should send only curl requests appears incompatible with this requirement. The next step is to verify whether they are using a Logitech Unifying receiver that stays on the Mac, or if they rely on the physical Easy-Switch hardware button instead.

Go or Python would suit a lightweight HTTP server. A thin wrapper around the existing mxswitch binary and BetterDisplay CLI seems cleanest. The display names and input labels still need confirmation.

BetterDisplay Version 5.0.5 Build 53495 - Integration Help

## General overview and syntax

The app supports the following integration methods:

- Command line integration
- Custom URL scheme based integration
- HTTP integration
- Notification based integration - for more details on this, see: https://betterdisplay.pro/integration
- macOS Shortcuts (App Intents)

The various integration methods can be separately enabled and disabled under Settings in the application UI.

An integration command might receive one or more operations and zero or more parameters. A parameter might or might not have a value associated with it.

### Syntax for command line access:

`./BetterDisplay operation [operation] [-parameter[=value]] [-parameter[=value]]`

Notes:

- The app binary `BetterDisplay` is available in the installed macOS app bundle (the full path when installed under `Applications` is `/Applications/BetterDisplay.app/Contents/MacOS/BetterDisplay`).
- You can use both single and double hyphen parameter style.

You can also use `betterdisplaycli` for simpler access. Installation via Homebrew:

`brew install waydabber/betterdisplay/betterdisplaycli`

Examples (both commands set the brightness of a display with the name `MyDisplay` to 80%):

`./BetterDisplay set -name=MyDisplay -brightness=0.8`

`betterdisplaycli set --name=MyDisplay --brightness=80%`

### Syntax for custom URL scheme integration:

`BetterDisplay://operation[/operation (…)][?parameter[=value]][&parameter[=value]]`

_**Agent (default)**_

BetterDisplay’s HTTP API on `:55777` is up, and `mxswitch` sees both **MX Keys B** and **MX Master 3S B** on Easy-Switch channel **2** (so Mac is almost certainly channel 2).

One design constraint matters before I write the plan: **Logitech ChangeHost can only be sent from the machine the devices are currently on.** So a Mac-only server can switch keyboard/mouse *to Windows* while you’re on the Mac, but when you’re on Windows and `curl` the Mac, the Mac **cannot** pull the Logitech devices back — they’re not talking to the Mac’s HID stack.

Two questions so the plan matches how you actually work:

1. **Logitech when switching from Windows → Mac** — which do you want?
   - **A)** Mac server only (display always switches via BetterDisplay; Logitech switches only when the devices are currently on the Mac — from Windows you’d use the Easy-Switch button, or a tiny Windows `mxswitch` later)
   - **B)** Also put a minimal Windows helper so `/mac` from Windows can move both display *and* Logitech (contradicts “Windows only needs curl”, but is the only way for full software control both directions)

2. **Channel + input mapping** — confirm:
   - Mac = Easy-Switch **2** + monitor **USB-C (`ddcAlt=465`)**
   - Windows = Easy-Switch **?** (1 or 3?) + monitor **HDMI (`ddcAlt=144`)**
   - Should the orchestration server bind on the LAN (e.g. `0.0.0.0:8080`) so Windows can reach it, or localhost-only plus something else?

_**Agent (default)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The user clarified the target mapping. The Mac server will handle requests to `/mac` and switch to HDMI 1 and channel 2. The Windows client will handle requests to `/windows` and switch to USBC and channel 1.

The Mac endpoint maps to HDMI 1 (ddcAlt=144) and channel 2. The Windows endpoint maps to USB-C (ddcAlt=465) and channel 1. This is unusual because the Mac typically uses USB-C while Windows uses HDMI. The current mxswitch state confirms the Mac is on channel 2 and the Windows device is on channel 1.

The Mac is the server executing all switches. A Logitech asymmetry complicates this: the Mac cannot send ChangeHost commands when devices are on Windows channel 1. The `/mac` endpoint only works when devices are already connected to the Mac. The `/windows` endpoint works because the devices are currently on the Mac.

BetterDisplay handles display switching bidirectionally. A curl to `/mac` from the Mac would switch the display to HDMI and channel 2, though the Logitech channel is already correct so no host change occurs. A curl to `/windows` would switch the display to USB-C and channel 1. The Mac endpoint is safe to call from the Mac itself.

A Python HTTP server using the standard library is the best fit. It avoids extra dependencies and can invoke the existing mxswitch binary directly. The server will listen on port 8080. Switching from Windows to Mac will fail silently for the Logitech host change, so the user will need the Easy-Switch button.

The server will launch BetterDisplay via `http://127.0.0.1:55777/set?ddcAlt=144&vcp=inputSelectAlt` and run the local `./mxswitch` binary. A small config file will hold the BetterDisplay URL, channel numbers, and DDC codes. An optional LaunchAgent can auto-start the server. The order of operations matters: switching Logitech first would drop the keyboard before the display changes, so the display switch should happen first.

The server will bind to 0.0.0.0 so the Windows client can reach it over the local network. Authentication is unnecessary for a home LAN.

The server code will live in a new `server/` directory inside the mxswitch repository. A LaunchAgent plist will handle persistence. The plan is now fully concrete with no remaining open options.
</details></think>

{
  "name": "Mac KVM HTTP server",
  "overview": "Add a small Mac-hosted HTTP server on :8080 that orchestrates BetterDisplay’s existing :55777 API and the local `mxswitch` binary, so `GET /mac` and `GET /windows` switch both the LG input and Logitech Easy-Switch channels.",
  "plan": "# Mac KVM HTTP controller\n\n## Goal\n\nRun a local orchestration server on the Mac (LAN-reachable) that Windows and Mac both hit with `curl`:\n\n| Endpoint | Monitor (BetterDisplay `:55777`) | Logitech (`mxswitch`) |\n|---|---|---|\n| `GET /mac` | HDMI — `ddcAlt=144` | channel **2** |\n| `GET /windows` | USB-C — `ddcAlt=465` | channel **1** |\n\nExamples:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://192.168.x.x:8080/mac\ncurl http://192.168.x.x:8080/windows\ncurl http://localhost:8080/mac\n```\n\n## Architecture\n\n```mermaid\nsequenceDiagram\n  participant Client as curl_Mac_or_Windows\n  participant Srv as KVM_server_8080\n  participant BD as BetterDisplay_55777\n  participant MX as mxswitch_binary\n\n  Client-\u003e\u003eSrv: GET /mac or /windows\n  Srv-\u003e\u003eBD: GET /set?ddcAlt=...\u0026vcp=inputSelectAlt\n  Srv-\u003e\u003eMX: mxswitch 2 or 1\n  Srv--\u003e\u003eClient: 200 JSON status\n```\n\nMac is the only machine that runs controllers. BetterDisplay already exposes HTTP; we do **not** reimplement DDC. Logitech uses the existing built [`macos/mxswitch.c`](macos/mxswitch.c) binary (switches both MX Keys + MX Master).\n\n**Known HID limit (documented, not a blocker for this build):** `mxswitch` can only ChangeHost while the devices are connected to the Mac. So `/windows` (leave to channel 1) works when you’re on the Mac. `/mac` always switches the display; Logitech returns to channel 2 only if the devices are still visible to the Mac (otherwise use the Easy-Switch button once, or call `/mac` before they leave).\n\n## Implementation choice\n\n**Python 3 stdlib only** — single file, no deps, ships with macOS.\n\nNew layout:\n\n- [`server/kvm_server.py`](server/kvm_server.py) — HTTP server\n- [`server/config.json`](server/config.json) — URLs, channels, ddc codes (edit without touching code)\n- [`server/com.mxswitch.kvm.plist`](server/com.mxswitch.kvm.plist) — LaunchAgent template for always-on\n- Short usage section in README or a `server/README.md`\n\n## Server behavior\n\n- Bind `0.0.0.0:8080` (LAN + localhost).\n- Routes: `/mac`, `/windows`, plus `/health` (liveness).\n- For each switch target:\n  1. Call BetterDisplay: `http://127.0.0.1:55777/set?ddcAlt={code}\u0026vcp=inputSelectAlt`\n  2. Run `mxswitch {channel}` (path from config, default `../mxswitch` or `$PATH`)\n  3. Return JSON: `{ \"ok\": true, \"target\": \"mac\", \"display\": \"...\", \"logitech\": \"...\" }` with clear errors if either step fails\n- Order: **display first, then Logitech** so the panel flips before the keyboard/mouse leave the Mac on `/windows`.\n- No auth (trusted home LAN). Easy to add a shared token later if needed.\n\nDefault [`server/config.json`](server/config.json):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"host\": \"0.0.0.0\",\n  \"port\": 8080,\n  \"betterdisplay_base\": \"http://127.0.0.1:55777\",\n  \"mxswitch_path\": \"../mxswitch\",\n  \"targets\": {\n    \"mac\": { \"ddc_alt\": 144, \"channel\": 2 },\n    \"windows\": { \"ddc_alt\": 465, \"channel\": 1 }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Run / install\n\n```bash\nmake                          # build mxswitch if needed\npython3 server/kvm_server.py  # foreground\n\n# optional always-on:\ncp server/com.mxswitch.kvm.plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/\n# edit ProgramArguments paths, then:\nlaunchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.mxswitch.kvm.plist\n```\n\nPrerequisites already on this machine: BetterDisplay HTTP integration enabled (`:55777`), Input Monitoring granted to `mxswitch`.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- No Windows-side scripts or Logitech software\n- No changes to BetterDisplay settings beyond calling its existing API\n- No rewrite of upstream mxswitch protocol code beyond using the binary\n",
